data.revised_prompt:
Edit the provided complex scientific figure into a cleaner publication-quality vector-like diagram for a computer science journal. Preserve the left-to-right data-flow and overall scientific active-depth / active stereo theme, but substantially simplify and declutter it. White background, crisp black arrows for forward sensing, red arrows for backward gradients, compact readable labels, balanced spacing, no decorative effects, no dense equations, no 3D shading.

Wide horizontal layout with four main regions from left to right:
1) Inputs / native geometry
2) Differentiable active-depth sensor response
3) Quality and validity formation
4) Observed outputs and gradient path

Title at top: "Differentiable active-depth model"

Left input block: a small active-stereo / IR projector schematic (simple, compact, less detailed than the original) labeled with "Native geometry renderer R" producing "D_raw". Include a small grayscale depth thumbnail. Add a nearby compact label "camera registers c=[P,E,G]" with three small chips: "P power", "E exposure", "G gain". Also add side inputs "scene / material mask Omega" and "speed ||v_t||" feeding the sensor response. Keep a small gray note near D_raw/Omega: "geometry and mask treated as fixed in sensor backward".

Center block: "S_phi" labeled "Differentiable sensor response". Inside or around it, show exactly five compact factor chips, no equations:
- "active return" with note "P, range"
- "ambient washout" with note "E, Omega"
- "motion blur" with note "E, ||v_t||"
- "gain / noise" with note "G"
- "edge difficulty" with note "depth discontinuity"
These factors merge into "quality Q" and then into "soft validity M". Include a small straight-through / hard-soft mask node labeled "hard forward, soft backward" or "straight-through mask".

Right side outputs: "observed depth D_obs" with a grayscale depth thumbnail, and "observed quality Q_obs" with a heatmap thumbnail. Add a small label near the gradient path from outputs back to registers: "L_sens / L_teach" and "gradient to P,E,G".

Important constraints:
- Use black arrows for forward flow and red arrows for backward gradients from L_sens / L_teach through D_obs, Q, M back to camera registers c=[P,E,G].
- Do NOT show backward gradients to D_raw or the geometry renderer.
- Do NOT include long formulas, inverse-square laws, sigmoid equations, or many small panels. Collapse regimes into "scene / material mask Omega".
- Keep only 3 or 4 total thumbnails, representative but minimal.
- Preserve a polished, readable figure at paper width.
- Keep the idea of active stereo / IR projector on the left, but small and less detailed.
- Avoid implying differentiable ray intersections.
- No arrows from Q or M into any policy module.

Make the diagram look like a simplified top-tier SCI journal method figure, clean vector-like, with compact labeled blocks and clearly separated regions.
